statement_record.book: f : x → y is (i) a monomorphism if fh = fk implies h = k for every parallel pair h,k : w → x (left cancellable); (ii) an epimorphism if hf = kf implies h = k for every parallel pair h,k : y → z (right cancellable). A monomorphism in C is exactly an epimorphism in C^op and conversely.

statement_record.book: Given x --s--> y --r--> x with rs = id_x: s is a section (right inverse) of r, r is a retraction (left inverse) of s, and x is a retract of y. Such an s is always a monomorphism and such an r is always an epimorphism; to record the one-sided inverse one calls s a split monomorphism and r a split epimorphism. Consequently an isomorphism is necessarily both monic and epic, though the converse fails (Exercise 1.2.iv).

statement_record.book: Exercise 1.2.v: (i) show f : x → y is a split epimorphism in C iff for every object c the postcomposition function f_* : C(c,x) → C(c,y) is surjective; (ii) argue by duality that f is a split monomorphism iff for every c the precomposition f^* : C(y,c) → C(x,c) is surjective.
statement_record.intree: Class Retraction `(f : x ~> y) := { retract : y ~> x; retract_comp : f ∘ retract ≈ id }.  Class Section `(f : x ~> y) := { section : y ~> x; section_comp : section ∘ f ≈ id }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the single probe object c = y (resp. c = x) is present. The classes assert exactly the book's condition instantiated at the identity — a chosen r with f ∘ r ≈ id is precisely a preimage of id_y under f_* — which is the crux of the exercise, but the ∀c form and the biconditional are never stated, so the easy generalization (given r, every g : c → y lifts as r ∘ g) is not available as a lemma. The library does know how to phrase such a condition: Construction/Localization.v:136 WLocal_surj states split-surjectivity of a precomposition map, `{ q : b ~> x & q ∘ w ≈ p }` for every p, for a different (locality) hypothesis; and Lib/Setoid.v:121 Class surjective := { surj {y} : { x & f x ≈ y} } is the split-surjectivity predicate that the book's 'surjective' would become here. Neither is connected to Retraction/Section. The duality half (ii) is likewise proved-by-symmetry in the book but written out independently in tree (Section and Retraction are separate classes, bridged only by flip_Section/flip_Retraction at Theory/Morphisms.v:230,241).

gap: No in-tree statement of the representable characterization: nothing asserts 'Retraction f ↔ ∀ c (g : c ~> y), { h : c ~> x & f ∘ h ≈ g }' (the surjectivity of f_* at every object c), nor its dual for Section and f^*. Only the c = y / c = x instance — the existence of the one-sided inverse — is formalized, as the definition of the classes themselves.
